text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts observed for /v1/generate across eu-west-1 and us-central-1. Error rate 5xx ~14% over last 3m. Provenance: frontend gateway -> router -> model-pool. Paging owners: @mike (oncall), @anya (backup). Links: https://metrics/redwood/alerts/4998001234, logs: https://logs/redwood/4998001234

mike: I’m on it. getting signal now. anyone see deploys?

eng-runtime: No deploys in last 30m. We see elevated latency to kv-prefix-cache nodes and a bunch of `ERR_KV_CORRUPT` logs from prefetch workers.

mike: copying logs, pasting head: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:01Z prefetch[worker-7] ERROR prefix_cache.go:412 prefix load failed key=mdl_abc:prefetch meta=checksum_mismatch
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z router[gw-12] WARN gateway.go:128 upstream=kv-prefix-cache time_ms=1532 status=504
2026-03-15T14:02:04Z runtime[pool-3] ERROR inference.go:89 kv lookup timeout err=context deadline exceeded
```

product-support: Is there noteworthy customer impact? Any 5xx higher for enterprise customers?

eng-runtime: Preliminary traffic analysis: All tiers affected, but dedicated pools see worse tail errors because they rely on prefix-cache warm paths. Hosted fallback routes show increased latency but fewer 5xx.

mike: ok mitigation plan proposal: 1) disable prefetch/pipeline for prefix-cache at edge (hotfix) 2) enable cache-bypass for model-pool routing -> route cold reads to S3-backed readthrough 3) scale kv-prefix-cache horizontally + bump timeouts 4) enable fallback model variant (lower mem) for canaryed flows. Anyone object?

anya: +1 from backup. I’ll take point on 2 and 3 if you do 1 and 4, mike.

mike: starting step 1 now: `/infra/rollout disable prefetch-prefix --clusters eu-west-1,us-central-1`

incident-bot: ACTION: prefetch prefix disabled in eu-west-1 (change-id: ch_49980_pf), us-central-1 pending.

mike: us-central-1 done. Observability: 5xx dropping to 6% but latency still high in some hosts.

eng-runtime: We’re seeing eviction storms on a subset of kv-prefix nodes (node-group: prefix-hot-12). Eviction rate spiked 1200% at 14:04: server logs show repeated rebalancing and compaction thrashing. Suspect checksum rot on disk leading to mis-indexed entries -> cache read paths crashing into validation errors.

dataplane-bot: NOTE: auto-scaling fired +3 instances for prefix-hot-12, but new instances also showing checksum_mismatch on startup (likely persisted state issue).

anya: we should avoid scaling up more stale nodes. Plan: drain and replace affected prefix-hot nodes, promote replica nodes without persisted state, and switch routing to bypass these shards. I’ll open a removal job.

mike: agreed. Launching shim to bypass prefix-hot-12: `/router/set-shard-policy --shard prefix-hot-12 --policy bypass-kv --duration 15m`

eng-runtime: shim applied. Traffic now routed through bypass to S3 readthrough for affected key ranges; seeing immediate drop in 5xx to ~2.1% and gateway timeouts down. Some increased token cost due to readthrough but customer impact reduced.

product-support: Noting customer-facing impact: a few customer support tickets for timeouts in chat features, highest severity on an enterprise tenant using Dedicated. Recommending an incident banner and support routing.

mike: I’ll open an incident banner draft. Ping me if you want wording. Also documenting mitigation: disabled prefetch, bypassed shard prefix-hot-12, prevented autoscale on that group.

product-support: Draft banner ok: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting text generation. Mitigations are in place; some users may experience delays. We will provide updates every 15 minutes." Approved.

eng-runtime: Live triage notes: root cause likely corrupted on-disk indexes on a subset of prefix-cache nodes triggered by a compaction+fs mismatch after a kernel upgrade last week. Repro: simulating compaction on staging with mixed kernel yields checksum_mismatch on restart.

anya: taking node replacement job. Steps: snapshot metadata, farm new ephemeral nodes, restore fresh caches, rehydrate via controlled prefetch (disabled globally) with integrity-check on writes. ETA ~22m.

mike: I’ll stay on pager for next 30m. @product-support, please gather list of affected enterprise tenants and severity.

product-support: On it. We have one P1 (acme-corp) reporting timeouts; others P2-P3. Escalating to sales as heads up.

eng-runtime: Patch recommended: add stricter checksum validation at prefetch time + safe-fallback to readthrough on validation failure (low-risk). Also plan a hotfix to make prefetch writes ephemeral until integrity verified. PR in flight: https://git/repo/pull/7891.

mike: Good. For immediate live mitigation we kept bypass in place and disabled pipeline. Any change in error rate after shard replacement?

dataplane-bot: UPDATE: prefix-hot-12 drained and decommissioned. New ephemeral nodes joined prefix-hot-12 replacement; initial health checks passed.

eng-runtime: After replacement, we re-enabled controlled prefetch for a small percentage (5%) with integrity checks. No checksum failures so far. Global re-enable deferred until full verification.

mike: 5xx now steady ~0.7% — falling back to normal. I’m going to annotate runbook and create a follow-up for postmortem: actions, timeline, customers impacted, root cause (on-disk index corruption + compaction/fs/kernel mismatch), and recommended rollout for hotfix PR.

anya: I’ll take the next shift (oncall handoff) at 14:25 UTC. mike you can go offline after you update PD notes.

mike: handing off. PD notes: mitigations applied (disabled prefetch, bypassed shard, drained/replaced nodes), customers notified, banner posted. Handing to @anya for postmortem writeup.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity lowered to SEV2. Next update in 30m unless status changes.

product-support: Support queue: open tickets for ACME-Corp P1, two midmarket P2s; shared banner and advised workarounds.

anya: taking. I’ll open the postmortem draft and start correlating logs and timeline. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks team, good triage. :thumbsup:
